messages:
oliver: heads up — trying to nail down the export handshake for audit exports (who changed what) so we can safely enable large-tenant downloads. main questions: signed URL lifetime, partial vs full payloads, and quota accounting. thoughts?

jia: for signed URLs i lean short-lived (1h) + one-time-use token for download. keeps S3 exposure low. longer if customer requests via contract.

sara: agree on short-lived links. also think we need two export modes in the API: "streaming-ndjson" (for SIEMs) and "bundle-archive" (zip with manifest). UI should show est size and token TTL before confirm.

mike: security note — if we allow full snapshots we must strip or pseudonymize sensitive actor fields unless tenant has approved sensitive export. otherwise add redaction level param.

oliver: +1 on redaction levels. proposal: export request includes {scope: tenant|org, redaction: none|pseudonymize|remove, mode: streaming|bundle, retention_override: optional}. backend validates caller perms and emits telemetry for cost/quota.

jia: how do we account quota? count tokens served for streaming, bytes for bundle? we need consistency so billing + quota tooling can rely on same metric.

sara: metric we expose: export_units where streaming = tokens/1000 (rounded up) and bundle = MB. Add labels: model=audit, redaction=level, requested_by=principal. That way console can break down cost/usage per export type.

mike: also emit provenance header in export (x-export-origin) with export_id so we can trace back for compliance. must be included in manifest for bundles and first line metadata for streaming.

export-bot: deploy-success: export-service v2.7.1 rolled to staging (canary 10%).

oliver: nice. on UI flow: show a staged preview that indicates example rows (first 10), with PII redaction toggles, and a checkbox for "I understand this export may contain sensitive events". record that acceptance in audit trail.

jia: for streaming NDJSON do we keep a continuous signed websocket or pre-signed POST streaming? webhooks are simpler for SIEMs. maybe offer both.

mike: webhooks require us to validate target endpoint and support retries/backoff. also we must limit replay window and log delivery attempts to telemetry.

sara: rollout plan: feature flag + enterprise opt-in. start with bundles only, keep redaction default to pseudonymize, telemetry sampling at 100% for errors and 10% for success for the first month.

oliver: action items: (1) jia to draft API shape + example request/response (2) mike to write security checklist for redaction & one-time tokens (3) sara to mock console preview and quota UX (4) i'll open RFC for export telemetry labels + billing mapping.

mike: I'll add export verification in pen-test plan.

oliver: thanks — i'll file the RFC and link here. rough timeline: staging tests next week, canary week after.

export-bot: ticket-created: EXPORT-RFC-221 linked https://go/repo/EXPORT-RFC-221

jia: ping when draft is up, i'll review the API ergonomics and sample payloads.

sara: i'll add a quick figma so we can validate the preview UX before dev.

oliver: perfect. if anyone thinks we should allow admins to schedule recurring exports, call it out now — otherwise keep out of MVP.

mike: keep out of MVP. stick to on-demand.

oliver: ok wrapping up here. thanks all :)
